title: Reliability roundtable — action items and handoff notes (2026-10-06)
summary: Notes from the 10/06 reliability roundtable covering three bounded incidents this week, SLO delta trends, runbook gaps, and explicit on-call handoff tasks.
content:
Context:
Quick sync after Friday’s on-call rotation. Goal: consolidate learnings from recent degradations and produce short actionable items to close before next rotation. Keep this doc lightweight — decisions, owners, and dates only.

High-level takeaways:
- Platform sustained 3 small-to-medium degradations this week; no P1s but customer-facing latency spikes for ~20–45 minutes in two events.
- Primary root cause patterns: (a) KV cache warmup + stampede on new model variant rollouts, (b) overloaded autoscaler edge case when scaling from 0 to burst, (c) a flaky healthcheck on multiplex-proxy that caused unnecessary instance churn.
- SLO drift: inference API availability fell from 99.97% to 99.92% for the rolling 7d window (target 99.95%). P95 latency increased from 280ms to 340ms during peak windows.

Incident summaries (brief):
1) KV-cache stampede — 2026-10-03 03:40 UTC
- Symptom: sudden increase in token-generation retries and 429s; clients saw retries and slightly duplicated responses.
- Impact: 15% increase in error-rate on hosted-api-route /v1/generate for 27 minutes; degraded A/B test buckets most.
- Root cause: simultaneous rollout of model-variant v3-alpha on 12 nodes; missing prefix-population and cache-miss amplification.
- Immediate mitigation: throttle rollout, enable conservative prefetch on new nodes, increase cache max-size by 20% for the cluster.
- Follow-ups: see action item A1.

2) Autoscaler cold-start storm — 2026-10-04 14:12 UTC
- Symptom: queue depth surged as scale-up started but new workers failed healthchecks intermittently, delaying readiness.
- Impact: p95 latency spike to ~620ms for 42 minutes; some large-batch customers observed timeouts.
- Root cause: race condition in readiness probe when kernel-level GPU drivers rebind slowly after network flakiness.
- Mitigation: temporarily pinned to reserve-capacity pool for affected accounts, and manually increased scale headroom.
- Follow-ups: see action item A2.

3) Multiplex-proxy flake — 2026-10-05 08:05 UTC
- Symptom: small but repeatable 503s from multiplex-proxy under spiky connect/disconnect patterns from streaming clients.
- Impact: short blips (5–10s) across multiple zones; aggregated to ~3.2% error-rate during spike windows.
- Root cause: edge connection tear-downs left ephemeral state in proxy causing backpressure and connection queue exhaustion.
- Mitigation: restart proxy pool nodes in affected AZs; applied temporary connection-rate limiter.
- Follow-ups: see action item A3.

SLO / Metrics snapshot:
- Rolling 7d availability (inference API): 99.92% (target 99.95%).
- Token-generation error-rate (client-facing): 0.85% baseline, spiked to 1.7% during incidents.
- p95 latency (global): baseline 280ms → spike 620ms during autoscaler event.
- Queue depth 99th percentile increased 4x during peak window.

Runbook gaps identified:
- Cache-rollout checklist incomplete: no canonical pre-warm step documented for model-variant transitions.
- Autoscaler healthcheck recipe not accounting for slow GPU driver binds; need a fallback readiness path.
- Multiplex-proxy health metrics missing a key gauge for "ephemeral-connection-state" which would have surfaced earlier.

Action items (owners, deadlines):
A1 — Cache rollout fixes (owner: Ethan Garcia) — due 2026-10-13
- Add pre-warm step to model rollout runbook: pre-populate KV prefixes for top-100 prefixes derived from production traces.
- Implement per-node startup backoff that staggers cache population windows by jitter up to 90s.
- Add alert: cache-miss-rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m during rollout -> page SRE oncall.
A2 — Autoscaler readiness hardening (owner: Marta Silva) — due 2026-10-11
- Add driver-bind timeout heuristics to readiness probe: treat prolonged driver rebind as "delayed-ready" instead of failing.
- Create a canary that runs node boot cycles in a simulated noisy network to catch regressions.
- Add documentation to infra-runbook: instructions for temporarily pinning affected customers to reserve-capacity.
A3 — Multiplex-proxy stabilization (owner: Henry Zhou) — due 2026-10-09
- Add connection-state metrics; emit an aggregated gauge for ephemeral-session-count and queue-latency.
- Implement defensive backpressure which drops the oldest streaming sessions when queue length exceeds thresholds; validate with load test.
- Implement automated rolling restart plan for proxies when ephemeral-session-count > X for 3 consecutive minutes.
A4 — SLO bridge playbook (owner: Priya Iyer) — due 2026-10-12
- Draft a short bridge playbook for small SLO dips (<0.1%) that includes quick mitigation steps and customer comms templates.
- Map SLO rollback triggers to specific runbook actions (e.g., model variant rollback, pin to reserve-capacity).

On-call handoff notes (next rotation: 2026-10-09 08:00 UTC):
- Incoming: Jorge (primary) / Linda (secondary). Outgoing: Priya.
- Key contexts to pass: A1 and A2 are in flight; Ethan and Marta will update PRs and runbook pages by respective due dates. Priya to leave a short bulleted checklist in rotation Slack thread when handing over.
- Known risk windows: scheduled small infra batch job on 2026-10-10 01:00 UTC that touches autoscaler metrics; advise to increase headroom that day.

Testing and verification plan:
- Run targeted chaos test for cache-stampede scenario on staging: create simultaneous 1000 cold requests against new variant while observing cache-miss amplification metric. (Owner: Ethan)
- Autoscaler canary job: start 10 replica nodes with simulated slow driver binds to validate readiness heuristics (Owner: Marta).
- Proxy load test: replay streaming connect/disconnect trace at 2x peak to validate backpressure changes (Owner: Henry).

Communications:
- Customer comms: on-call to prepare a short status update post-mitigations if SLO remains degraded more than 24h. Template is in CONFLUENCE-7421.
- Internal: ship a short postmortem-lite for the KV-cache stampede (not a full P1) — assigned to Ethan, due 2026-10-15.

Notes / Misc (freeform):
- Quick idea: consider a lightweight global prefix-populator service that streams top prefixes from runtime traces to new nodes. Might be a Q1 project; capture in product backlog (ticket: SRE-PREFILL-Q1).
- Reminder: keep runbook changes minimal and tested; avoid adding complex warmup logic without load tests.

Next sync:
- Quick async check-in on action-item statuses in #sre-ops 2026-10-09 morning; full reliability roundtable on 2026-10-13 to validate progress and decide whether to escalate to a P1-style review.

- Autoscaler failure cluster log: s3://redwood-ops-logs/autoscaler/2026-10-04/cluster-57.log
- Multiplex-proxy PR for temp limiter: github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/178

End of notes.
